--- title: "[Surv]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A survival response, built exactly as R's `survival::Surv()` builds one. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_surv.py#L207-L818){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Surv(time, time2=None, event=None, *, type=None, origin=0.0) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `Surv()` records a time-to-event outcome in one of R's forms. The type is inferred from the arguments, as in R: - `Surv(time, event)` is right-censored. `event` may be logical, `0`/`1`, or `1`/`2` (as in the `lung` data, where `2` means died). - `Surv(start, stop, event)` is a counting-process response, for late entry (left truncation) and time-varying covariates. - A categorical `event` (a pandas or Polars categorical, or an Arrow dictionary) gives a multi-state response, whose first level means censored. - `type="left"`, `type="interval"`, and `type="interval2"` must be asked for. Status values R doesn't accept become missing, with a warning. Missing values are kept, and rows with any missing value are dropped when a model is fitted. For exact, right-, left-, and interval-censored data, `event_time()` is often clearer, and `as_surv()` converts it. `Surv()` takes values: lists, arrays, or series already in hand. To start from a data frame, name the columns instead, in a formula such as `"Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age"` or with `Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status == 2")`, and pass `data=` to `fit()`. That form is evaluated on the frame's own backend, so it works the same on pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, and lazy frames. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Follow-up time for right-censored data, or the start time for counting-process data, or the lower bound for interval data. Numeric, with `None` or `nan` for missing values. [time2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stop time for counting-process data, or the upper bound for interval data. When `event` is not given and `type` is not an interval type, a second argument is the status (R's rule), so `Surv(time, status)` works positionally. [event]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The status. Logical, `0`/`1`, or `1`/`2` for right, left, and counting data. Codes `0` (right), `1` (exact), `2` (left), and `3` (interval) for `type="interval"`. A categorical for a multi-state response. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : One of `"right"`, `"left"`, `"interval"`, `"counting"`, `"interval2"`, or `"mstate"`. The default infers `"right"` or `"counting"` from the number of arguments. [origin]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Subtracted from every time, as in R. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a time or the status isn't of a type R accepts. The messages match R's. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If lengths differ, or the arguments don't fit the requested type. ::: ## Warns {.doc-warns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [UserWarning]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : When status values are invalid or intervals run backwards. Those rows become missing, as in R. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Four subjects: events at times 5 and 4, censored at 6 and 9: ::: {#fc1f776e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Surv(time=[5, 6, 4, 9], event=[1, 0, 1, 0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Surv(type=right, n=4, events=2) ``` ::: ::: `1`/`2` status coding works as it does in R, where `2` means an event: ::: {#36271cfb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} gw.Surv(time=[5, 6, 4, 9], event=[2, 1, 2, 1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` Surv(type=right, n=4, events=2) ``` ::: ::: A start time gives a counting-process response: ::: {#f4d8ccfa .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} gw.Surv(time=[0, 2, 1], time2=[5, 6, 4], event=[1, 0, 1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Surv(type=counting, n=3, events=2) ``` ::: ::: A categorical status gives a multi-state response, with the first level meaning censored: ::: {#07853d82 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd outcome = pd.Categorical( ["death", "censor", "relapse", "death"], categories=["censor", "relapse", "death"] ) gw.Surv(time=[5, 6, 7, 8], event=outcome) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Surv(type=mright, n=4, events=3, states=('relapse', 'death')) ``` ::: ::: Interval data uses R's coding, or lower and upper bounds with `type="interval2"`: ::: {#11eb42b9 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np # The event happened in (1, 2], after 2, and in (3, 5] gw.Surv(time=[1, 2, 3], time2=[2, np.inf, 5], type="interval2") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` Surv(type=interval, n=3, events=2) ``` ::: ::: Starting from a data frame, name the columns and let `fit()` read them. We'll use the bundled `pbc` dataset, from a Mayo Clinic trial in primary biliary cholangitis, where `status` is `0` (censored), `1` (transplant), or `2` (died): ::: {#72478e44 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} pbc = gw.load_dataset("pbc") # The same as Surv(time, status == 2) in R, evaluated on the frame's own backend gw.CoxPH().fit("Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + bili", data=pbc) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` CoxPH (Cox proportional hazards model, ties='efron') coef exp(coef) se(coef) z p age 0.04313 1.044 0.008055 5.354 8.594e-08 bili 0.1436 1.154 0.01142 12.578 2.8e-36 n = 418, events = 161 Likelihood ratio test = 126.1 on 2 df, p = 4.097e-28 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
entry Entry time of each row: the start time for counting data, otherwise $-\infty$.
event Whether each row has an event (any state, for multi-state data).
is_multistate Whether the response has several event states.
is_truncated Whether rows have start times (late entry).
lower The `time1` column for interval data, otherwise `None`.
n Number of rows.
n_censored Number of censored rows (status `0`).
n_events Number of rows with an event.
start Start times for counting-process data, otherwise `None`.
states State names for a multi-state response (status `k` is `states[k - 1]`), otherwise
status The status column, as floats with `nan` for missing values, as R stores it.
stop The (stop) time column: `time` for right and left data, `stop` for counting data, and
type The response type, one of R's type names (see `CensoringType`).
